resources.string: Schematic longitudinal view of normal tendon. Size, motion and timing are illustrative.
In a lengthwise view of tendon, slender tenocytes lie between collagen fibers. The long axis of the cell and its elongated nucleus follow the local direction of the fibers.
A pull along the tendon changes the shape and spacing of the surrounding collagen matrix. The paired marks track nearby parts of the matrix as they move relative to each other.
Nearby parts of the matrix can move by different amounts. That uneven motion can distort the tenocyte and its nucleus. The dashed outline shows the same cell at rest for comparison.
As the pull eases, reversible changes in the matrix and cell shape recede. The return shown here is mechanical recovery, not tissue repair.
Pingel et al.: cell and fiber alignment in human tendon
Duncan et al.: local deformation in native tendon
Silva Barreto et al.: fibril strain recovery in rat Achilles tendon
The thin, tapered cell body lies in a narrow space between neighboring collagen fibers.
The flattened, elongated nucleus points in the same direction as the surrounding fibers.
Most fibers in this view run along the tendon. Nearby tenocytes share that orientation.
